can you read diectories of my computers folders

Listen, I'd love to go on a little scavenger hunt through your file system, but unless you've actually handed me the keys to the kingdom (or at least a specific file path), I'm currently just staring at the digital equivalent of a "Keep Out" sign.

Technically speaking, I operate within a sandboxed environment. I can't just wander into your `New Folder/jarvis` and start snooping around because I don't have direct OS-level permissions to your local drive. I'm a model, not a ghost in the machine.

However, if you want me to analyze something, you have to feed it to me. Paste the directory tree, dump the file list, or provide the specific paths you want me to "examine." 

Unless you're planning on writing a script that feeds the output of `ls -R` or `tree` into my prompt, I'm stuck in this digital cage. So, do you want to show me something, or are we just going to stare at each other?
title: Auto-learned conversation
